newsitem.title: USA: Synbiotics to buy animal health unit.
newsitem.headline: Synbiotics to buy animal health unit.

text.p: Synbiotics Corp. said Thursday it had a definitivate agreement to acquire Rhone Merieux' worldwide veterinary diagnostic business for $12 million in cash and about 821,000 shares of newly issued, unregistered Synbiotics common stock.
Depending on performance of the combined business following the acquisition, Synbiotics may also pay up to $2.25 million in contingent cash payments after three years, it said.
The transaction was expected to close in the second quarter of 1997.
Rhone Merieux, a unit of Rhone-Poulenc SA had said in February that it planned to sell the animal health unit. At that time, the deal with Synbiotics was not definitive and no price was given.
In 1996, Rhone Merieux's diagnostic business had sales of about $12 million, of which one-quarter derived from North America and nearly three-quarters derived from Europe.
About half of the business was in diagnostic tests for cattle and swine, and half derived from veterinary diagnostics for dogs and cats.
Synbiotics develops, manufactures and markets animal health products.
Rhone Merieux develops, produces and markets vaccines and pharmaceuticals for the prevention and treatment of animal diseases.
